title: She knocked on the wrong door
lesson: If you know someone who is alone this Christmas, knock. You never know who is on the other side.

beats.vo: Three Christmases ago, a girl knocked on the wrong door. She's the reason I'm baking tonight.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot from inside an apartment as the white door is already open: Mia stands in the lit stairwell holding a white plate of uneven homemade sugar cookies in both hands, her face clearly visible, she smiles warmly and opens her mouth to say hello, a few snowflakes melting on her green sleeves and red scarf, one stairwell lamp. Soft stairwell ambience and the rustle of her scarf.

beats.vo: It's Christmas Eve, and she lands in two hours. So let me tell you how we met.
beats.shot: Close-up of the girl's hands pressing a star-shaped cutter into rolled gingerbread dough on a floured pale wood worktop, snow falling past the window behind, bright soft daylight. The soft press of the cutter in the dough.

beats.vo: I'd just moved to this city for a new job. I didn't know a single person here.
beats.shot: The girl seen from behind standing still at a tall apartment window, looking out at a snowy city street with rooftops, one mug of tea in her hands, steam rising, bright white winter daylight. The quiet of snow.

beats.vo: My family was far away, and flights in December? Way too expensive.
beats.shot: Close-up of the girl's hands cracking one single egg into a large empty cream ceramic bowl on a pale wood worktop, snow outside the window. The crack of the shell and the egg sliding into the bowl.

beats.vo: So I told everyone I was fine. Just a quiet Christmas on my own.
beats.shot: The girl seen from the side, head bowed, eyes on the bowl, slowly whisking the egg with a fork at the worktop, snow falling past the window, bright soft daylight. The gentle tap of the fork against the bowl.

beats.vo: On Christmas Eve, I made a tiny pot of soup. Enough for one.
beats.shot: Evening. Close-up of a small pot of orange carrot soup simmering on a stove, steam rising, one cream bowl and one spoon waiting beside it, the window behind is deep blue dusk with snow. The soft bubbling of the soup.

beats.vo: Then someone knocked. I almost didn't open it.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot in a small apartment entryway: the girl in her cream cardigan and apron walks to the plain white front door, hesitates for a second, then opens it with an easy natural movement, seen from the side, one warm hallway lamp. Her soft footsteps and the door opening.

beats.vo: There was a girl in a red scarf, holding a plate of cookies.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot from inside the doorway: Mia stands in the lit stairwell holding a white plate of uneven homemade sugar cookies, her face clearly visible, cheerful, a few snowflakes melting on her green sweater and long red scarf, she lifts the plate a little as she speaks. Soft stairwell ambience.

beats.vo: She said, Merry Christmas, Mrs. Patel! And I'm not Mrs. Patel.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium close shot of Mia at the open apartment door holding the plate of cookies, her face clearly visible: she starts to say something cheerfully, then realises her mistake, her eyes widen and she laughs in embarrassment, pressing the back of her free hand to her mouth. Soft laughter and stairwell ambience.

beats.vo: Mrs. Patel lived upstairs. She'd got the wrong floor.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot in the open apartment doorway: Mia, face clearly visible, laughing, points up the staircase with her free hand while holding the plate of cookies, the girl in the cream cardigan stands inside the door laughing too, both faces visible in profile, one stairwell lamp. Soft shared laughter.

beats.vo: We both laughed. It was so awkward. Then she looked past me, at my one little bowl of soup.
beats.shot: Evening. A small kitchen table with one cream bowl of orange carrot soup and one spoon, steam rising, an empty chair, the window behind deep blue dusk with snow, the small tree's warm-white string lights in the corner. Quiet room tone.

beats.vo: And she said, hey, are you doing anything tonight?
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot over the girl's shoulder in the doorway: Mia stands in the stairwell holding the plate of cookies, her face clearly visible, friendly and a little shy, tilting her head and asking a question, the girl's chestnut braid in the foreground, warm hallway lamp. Soft hallway ambience.

beats.vo: I said no. Honestly, I was too embarrassed to lie.
beats.shot: Evening. Close-up of the girl's hands slowly untying her beige linen apron and folding it over a chair back, the tree's warm-white string lights soft in the background. The soft rustle of linen.

beats.vo: Twenty minutes later I was upstairs in Mrs. Patel's kitchen, with six people I'd never met.
beats.shot: Evening. Wide shot from a kitchen doorway of a busy family kitchen table seen from behind the guests' shoulders, several hands passing bowls of food and a basket of bread across the table, steam rising from dishes, one ceiling lamp, snow at the dark window. The happy clatter of plates and cutlery.

beats.vo: Her name was Mia. She talked a lot, and she laughed louder than anyone.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot in a warm family kitchen: Mia stands at the stove stirring a pot, her face clearly visible in three-quarter view, talking and laughing loudly at something someone off-screen said, steam rising, one ceiling lamp, snow at the dark window. The spoon in the pot and warm laughter.

beats.vo: She handed me a knife and said, you're on potatoes. Like I'd always been there.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot at a kitchen counter: Mia, face clearly visible, laughing, slides a big bowl of unpeeled potatoes along the counter to the girl in the cream cardigan and gives her a playful nudge with her shoulder; the girl laughs and starts to roll up her sleeves, both faces visible, warm kitchen lamp. The bowl sliding on the counter and soft laughter.

beats.vo: I don't think she ever knew what that did for me.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot of Mia and the girl standing side by side at a kitchen sink rinsing potatoes under the tap, turned toward each other, talking easily and laughing, both faces visible in profile, water running, steam from a pot behind, warm kitchen lamp. Running water and easy chatter.

beats.vo: After that night, she just kept showing up.
beats.shot: Bright daylight. Medium shot of Mia and the girl sitting cross-legged on a sofa by a big window with snow falling, each holding a mug of tea, turned toward each other, talking and laughing freely, Mia gesturing with her free hand, both faces visible. Soft laughter and the quiet of snow.

beats.vo: Sunday pancakes. Terrible movies. Long walks when work got hard.
beats.shot: Close-up of a pancake being flipped in a small pan on a stove, golden on top, butter sizzling, bright morning daylight from a snowy window. The sizzle and the soft flip.

beats.vo: When I got sick in February, she left soup at my door every single day.
beats.shot: Close-up of Mia's hands in green knit sleeves setting a glass jar of orange soup with a cloth lid tied with string on a doormat in front of a plain white apartment door, morning light in the hallway. The soft clink of the jar on the floor.

beats.vo: And she never once made it feel like a favor.
beats.shot: Close-up of the girl's hands tying a thin red ribbon around a small glass jar of homemade cookies on a pale wood worktop, bright soft daylight, snow outside. The whisper of the ribbon.

beats.vo: Later I found out she was new here too. Only a year before me.
beats.shot: Mia sitting alone on a windowsill seat with her knees pulled up, seen from the side so her face is visible in profile, calm and thoughtful, looking out at falling snow over the rooftops, short black bob, green sweater, red scarf, bright grey-white daylight. The hush of snow.

beats.vo: She knew exactly how that first Christmas feels.
beats.shot: Close-up of snowflakes falling slowly past a window, a single mug of tea on the sill steaming, the quiet street blurred far below. The soft hush of snow.

beats.vo: That plate of cookies wasn't really for Mrs. Patel. It was her excuse to knock on doors.
beats.shot: Close-up of the girl's hands arranging uneven homemade gingerbread stars on a white plate one by one, a little flour on the worktop, bright soft daylight. The light tap of cookies on the plate.

beats.vo: She told me that last year, laughing, with flour all over her face.
beats.shot: Bright daylight. Medium shot of Mia and the girl kneading gingerbread dough together at a floured pale wood worktop, Mia with a smudge of flour on her cheek, both laughing freely at it, the girl wiping it off with the back of her wrist, both faces visible. Soft laughter and the push of the dough.

beats.vo: This spring, Mia moved away for the job she'd always wanted.
beats.shot: Close-up of Mia's hands with the silver ring pressing tape along the top of a cardboard moving box on a wooden floor, bright spring daylight. The long rip of packing tape.

beats.vo: I cried at the airport. Then I called her from the car.
beats.shot: The girl seen from behind sitting in a parked car, her hands resting on the steering wheel, looking out through the windscreen at a grey airport parking lot, perfectly calm and still, soft overcast light. Quiet car interior.

beats.vo: So tonight, she's flying back. Just for Christmas. Just for this.
beats.shot: Close-up of the girl's hands in oven mitts lifting a tray of dark-edged gingerbread stars out of the oven, a little steam, bright late afternoon daylight from a snowy window. The oven door and the tray on the worktop.

beats.vo: I'm making her favorite. Gingerbread, a little burnt on the edges, the way she likes it.
beats.shot: Close-up of uneven gingerbread stars with slightly dark edges cooling on a wire rack, a little steam rising, snow falling past the window behind. Quiet kitchen tone.

beats.vo: And there's one more thing I'm doing this year.
beats.shot: The girl seen from the side, head bowed, eyes on the small card, writing a few words with a pen on a plain brown gift tag at the kitchen table, bright soft daylight. The scratch of the pen.

beats.vo: There's a new girl on the second floor. She moved in last month.
beats.shot: Evening. A quiet apartment building hallway with a plain closed door that has no wreath, a single doormat, one ceiling lamp, snow at the small window at the end. Quiet hallway tone.

beats.vo: So I made her a plate too.
beats.shot: Close-up of the girl's hands wrapping a white plate of gingerbread stars in clear paper and tying it with a thin red ribbon and the brown tag, the tree's warm-white string lights soft in the background. The crinkle of paper.

beats.vo: Because once, someone knocked on my door. And it changed everything.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot in a quiet apartment building hallway: the girl in her cream cardigan stands in front of a plain white door with no wreath, holding a plate of gingerbread wrapped in clear paper with a red ribbon, she takes a small breath and smiles softly, seen from the side so her face is visible, one ceiling lamp. A soft knock on wood and hallway quiet.

beats.vo: If you know someone who's alone this Christmas, knock. Even if it feels awkward.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot from the hallway: a plain white apartment door is open, a young woman of about 24 with long straight light-brown hair and a grey hoodie stands inside, surprised and then smiling shyly as the girl in the cream cardigan, seen in profile, holds out the wrapped plate of gingerbread, warm room light spilling into the hallway. Soft hallway ambience.

beats.vo: You never know who's on the other side.
beats.shot: Evening. Medium shot of Mia and the girl sitting side by side on a sofa by a big window with snow falling outside, turned toward each other, talking and laughing freely, Mia's hand on the girl's arm as she laughs, both faces visible, two mugs, the small tree's warm-white string lights beside them. Soft laughter and room tone.

beats.vo: Merry Christmas.
beats.shot: Evening. Close-up of two mugs of hot cider clinking gently together in front of a window with snow falling outside, the girl's hand and Mia's hand with the silver ring, the small tree's warm-white string lights soft in the background. The clink of the mugs.
